quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts you and the rider in danger. If the rider falls, you need space to avoid hitting them. Falls are more likely on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: When driving in fog, it is best to drive with:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped ahead of you in your lane with its red lights flashing. You should:

options.text: Stop and proceed when you think all of the children have exited the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.
Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip on gravel and dirt than on paved roads. Slow down on these surfaces. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: You should signal at least how many feet before you turn?
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. On freeways, signal at least five seconds before changing lanes. Always signal before pulling to or away from the curb, even if no other vehicles are nearby. Turn off your signal when you no longer need it.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the effects of alcohol will be reduced only by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time reduces alcohol's effects in your body. Coffee, cold showers, or exercise do not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and do not tailgate.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Upcoming change in direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Which of these statements is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check all mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the next lane is clear and there are no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles nearby.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Drive with caution near railroad tracks.

questions.question: When a pedestrian guided by a dog or carrying a white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A blind or partially blind pedestrian may use a guide dog or carry a white cane. Always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: You must notify the DMV within five days if you:

options.text: Sell or transfer your vehicle.
Fail a smog test.
Get a new prescription for lenses or contacts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sell or transfer your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Report a vehicle sale or transfer to the DMV within five days.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, check your rearview mirror for both headlights of the car you passed. Only then is it safe to return to your original lane.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk and in rain or snow, it can be hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:

options.text: Up the instrumental panel lights.
On your parking lights.
On your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: On your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever visibility is poor or other drivers cannot see you. Turn on headlights if weather requires you to use windshield wipers. Always use low beams.

questions.question: If a motorist sees pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should the motorist do?

options.text: Continue ahead. The motorist has the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. Wait until the pedestrians have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: Children on bicycles should be given extra space by motor vehicle operators because:

options.text: They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may suddenly move onto the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly in front of their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your vehicle—to the sides, ahead, and behind. Good drivers know what is happening in all directions around their car.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, your right, then your left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, your right, then your left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. Look for vehicles and pedestrians. Check left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer than those from your right. Look all the way across the intersection to make sure the path is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Right turn on red light permitted with caution.
All traffic must turn right at next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line over a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can harm your judgment and coordination. You do not need to reach the legal limit to be impaired. Driving with any alcohol in your blood can lead to criminal charges.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than regular cars. At 55 mph, a car can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: All of these are dangerous while driving. Which one is also illegal?

options.text: Wearing a headset that covers both ears
Having one or more interior lights on
Using cruise control on residential streets

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a headset that covers both ears
questions.explanation: It is illegal to wear a headset or earplugs in both ears while driving. You need to hear all sounds around you to stay safe.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: To speed up slightly.
That it is not safe to pass.
To maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass another vehicle in that area. These zones exist in places where you cannot see far ahead, making passing unsafe.

questions.question: You want to turn right at an upcoming intersection. You should slow down and:

options.text: Move toward the left side of your lane.
Avoid driving in the bicycle lane.
Signal for 100 feet before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal for 100 feet before turning.
questions.explanation: Start signaling about 100 feet before you make a right turn.

questions.question: What happens if you misuse a disabled parking placard?

options.text: Placard revocation only.
Only a fine.
Placard revocation, a fine, and/or jail time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placard revocation, a fine, and/or jail time.
questions.explanation: Misusing a disabled placard is a crime. You can lose your placard, pay a fine of up to $1,000, and spend up to six months in jail.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough for your vehicle.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
Only under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. Drive at safe speeds that match the weather, traffic, and road conditions.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs affect driving, including prescription sedatives and tranquilizers, over-the-counter cold and cough medicines, and illegal drugs. Check medicine labels for warnings before driving.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and grip the wheel firmly. Take your foot off the accelerator and let the car slow down. Gently apply the brakes when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian on the road, but an oncoming vehicle is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one road hazard at a time. If an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let it pass. Then pass the pedestrian only when it is safe.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together to protect you. Always wear your seat belt, even in a car with airbags.

questions.question: Following another car too closely (tailgating):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents being "cut off."

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is a risky behavior that can lead to aggressive driving. Drivers can receive traffic citations for tailgating.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, you should:

options.text: Turn up the radio loudly so you won't think about it while driving.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving safety. If you are angry, upset, worried, or depressed, calm down before you drive. You need to focus fully on driving.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percent of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Try to fight it.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop driving and take a break if you feel tired. Rest, nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for sleep.

questions.question: Which is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Tailgating another vehicle
Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, drive at a safe speed, do not follow other cars too closely, and pay attention to workers and equipment.
